cut_items.item: Single combined command sequence including stopping running containers first before prune
Explicit note that the prune command also removes build cache and that the Docker Engine 25+ caveat applies to --volumes (anonymous only); gives docker volume prune -a -f

Stops running containers first with `docker stop $(docker ps -q)` so a single prune command can clean up everything, including the stopped containers (this answers the user's 'delete all' intent directly)
Pairs docker volume prune -a -f to remove named volumes, with the version caveat

added_items.item: Clarifies that docker system prune -a --volumes keeps running containers and the images/volumes they use (X's stop-first step makes it wipe everything, but Y states the actual behavior)
Docker Desktop on Mac/Windows: virtual disk file doesn't shrink on its own; use Settings > Resources disk image size or Clean/Purge data
Troubleshooting: 'volume is in use' and 'image is being used' errors, remove the container first
Per-type targeted cleanup commands (container prune, image prune dangling vs -a, volume prune, builder prune -a)
docker builder prune -a -f in the full-wipe sequence to clear build cache
Distinguishes quick prune (unused only) from full wipe including running containers, with warning scoped to the destructive full wipe
Confirmation prompt behavior (y to confirm, -f to skip)
Identifies the empty-list error message text ('requires at least 1 argument') and says to skip that command
Explanation of dangling images (untagged layers) vs all unused images
docker rm -f runs after docker stop with -aq (covers stopped containers too)
Run `docker system df` before cleanup to check usage (Y mentions before and after)
Prune command keeps running containers and the images and volumes they use
Confirmation prompt: type y, or use -f to skip it
Explicit warning that deleted data is unrecoverable (Y also has this)
Docker 23+ caveat that --volumes may remove only anonymous volumes, with docker volume prune -a for named ones (Y gives a similar caveat tied to Engine 25)
Full wipe sequence also includes `docker builder prune -a -f` for build cache
Explains the 'requires at least 1 argument' error means the list is empty and can be skipped (Y says the error is harmless)
Per-type prune commands: docker container prune, docker image prune (dangling), docker image prune -a, docker volume prune, docker builder prune -a
Docker Desktop on Mac/Windows: the virtual disk file does not shrink on its own, so use Settings > Resources > Disk image size or Clean/Purge data
Troubleshooting: 'volume is in use' or 'image is being used' errors mean you must remove the container using it first
Lists exactly what system prune removes, including that it covers networks and build cache
Explicit warning to back up database or upload data before the full wipe
